Marissa / Neha —

Quick update and attached preliminary results (acme-eval-results-prelim-20260714.pdf). High level:
- Models tested: open-llm-v1 int8 (Redwood), cloudx-llm-3 (hyperscaler).
- Latency (short prompts): Redwood p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 280ms; CloudX p50 ~ 140ms, p95 ~ 420ms. Our batching + KV cache helped for repeat queries.
- Quality (200 prompts + 50 billing prompts):
  - Correct: Redwood 84% vs CloudX 82%
  - Partially correct: Redwood 9% vs CloudX 10%
  - Incorrect / hallucination: Redwood 7% vs CloudX 8%
- Instruction-following test: Redwood passed 96% of short stop-token cases; CloudX passed 91%.
- Cost estimate (approx): Redwood $0.95 per 1M tokens (with quantized profile + batching), CloudX $1.60 per 1M tokens. Estimates include infra + model runtime (no discounts).

Notes / caveats:
- CloudX results were run with their default decoding; we should run a second CloudX pass with lower temperature and nucleus decoding to see if hallucination rate improves — will schedule if you want.
- The billing prompt subset contained some redacted items; we used synthetic placeholders that matched the structure for fairness. If Acme provides the real sensitive subset we should re-run the billing prompts on the final pass.

Next steps I suggest:
- Share the attached preliminary PDF in Monday's sync and walk through the p95 latency tradeoffs.
- If Acme wants, run CloudX with alternative decoding params (low temp + top_p=0.9) and re-run the billing subset once provided.

Attaching a small appendix with example failure cases and hallucination transcripts. Happy to pair on the slide pack.

Aditya
